narrative: A 23-year-old from the southern Syrian city of Deraa set out for Europe through Libya. A smuggler had promised him only a ten-day stay in Libya before a boat to Italy, but it stretched into more than eight months spent between detention centers, smuggling dens and hangars he likened to torture chambers. He was beaten, sold and humiliated, and after each failed attempt to leave he was sold on and moved from place to place - Tobruk, Derna, Benghazi, Gazala - held in disease-ridden warehouses with hundreds of other men under the violent control of armed guards. Beatings and humiliating searches for phones were a daily routine; anyone caught contacting the outside world was struck with stones or guns until they lost consciousness. He spoke of people randomly detained and forced to pay to get out, often with money they did not have, and of places known for humiliation, violence and torture, from which it was nearly impossible to leave once detained. He was eventually rescued in the middle of the Mediterranean, and hoped for a life beyond the violence.
